input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 is the only right of inspection running against us. Notice (30 days), business-hours conduct and cost allocation (HDI bears its own inspection fees, with no underpayment shift-back) already meet or exceed the preferred position, and the right is limited to payment-calculation records held by our General Manager, so there is no access to Company systems. However, the clause contains no frequency limit at all, leaving HDI free to inspect repeatedly — unlimited audits fall below the fallback (once per year) and into walk-away territory. We therefore made the minimal edit of a once-per-twelve-month cap. That the inspector is HDI's General Manager rather than an independent auditor is noted but not separately flagged, since HDI is already bound by the confidentiality obligations in Section 8.2.

ops.oldText: may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company
ops.newText: may, no more than once in any twelve (12) month period and upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a once-per-twelve-month cap on HDI's inspection right, as the clause is currently unlimited in frequency; the existing 30 days' notice, business-hours limitation and HDI cost-bearing are acceptable and unchanged.
proposal.summary: Cap HDI's records inspection right at once per twelve months
